rv.q: Like many pre-Broadway tryouts, it has its strengths and weaknesses and a wildly uneven second half of a second act that suggests everyone simply ran out of enough time to fashion an ending that really satisfies.
Ghee as The Lady Chablis is the real beating heart in MIDNIGHT OF THE GARDEN OF GOOD AND EVIL, but otherwise the musical's score and character arcs need refinement to really come into focus.
This is one of the best new musicals I've seen in a long time, and I suspect it will have a long and successful run when it ultimately comes to Broadway.
This is a show that lingers long after the curtain falls. It's a dazzling spectacle, a love letter to the captivating city of Savannah.
I'm going to bet with a bit of heavy pruning this garden will be a hit.
'Midnight' is a sparkling, engaging night at the theater, and will make you want to book a weekend in Savannah.

While Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil doesn't quite feel completely comfortable in its new musical stage adaptation, what Mac and Brown have concocted is certainly smart, stylistically impressive and extremely entertaining.
Each one of these conflicts is served well by Brown's rather tasty score which, if written with clashing styles, are held together by his piano-driven jazz-funk imprimatur.
There's a good mixture of the funny and the dramatic packed into this moody, eye-popping production, but there's little final payoff at the end.
And yet 'Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil' — buoyed by A-list creatives and a top-notch cast — has potential. Realizing that potential requires some work.
These sections feel both forced and out of place to the point that the eventual message of equality that is trying to find a light of its own lacks the necessary inspirational spark.
I believe this musical is worth seeing for J. Harrison Ghee as The Lady Chablis alone.
MIDNIGHT IN THE GARDEN OF GOOD AND EVIL The Musical is less good and evil and more fun and dull.
Too many changes are needed to make this production successful, but it has the ingredients to shine — as it stands now, without J. Harrison Ghee, the musical, is dead on arrival.
Without a doubt 'Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil' is the best musical I have seen in years.
Not just highly recommended; but gets the HIGHEST of Recommendations…this show is NOT to be missed!
I left the theatre feeling elated, my faith in humanity restored. I loved the music, I loved the performances, and I loved the message.
